input.rationale: Only 3 merit measurements were available, so I targeted the Fe-V-rich, Ni-poor corner, where FeVO4-type phases are expected to be the photoactive absorbers under 3.2 eV light. Index 34 (Fe0.39 Ni0.18 V0.42), which is close to 1:1 Fe:V, gave the highest photocurrent (2.8 µA). A more Fe-rich point (158) and a more V-rich point (94) were both lower, so the local maximum is near Fe:V ≈ 1.

rejected.reason: V-rich beyond FeVO4 stoichiometry: measured 1.87 µA, lower than 34
Ni oxides/vanadates are expected to be poor photoanode absorbers; not worth spending the 3-measurement budget there

content.text:
The episode is finished. I submitted **index 34 (Fe 0.39, Ni 0.18, V 0.42)** as the best composition, with a photocurrent of **2.8 µA**.

The budget allowed only 3 photocurrent measurements, so I spent them all in the Fe- and V-rich, Ni-poor part of the library. I expected that region to do best because of FeVO₄-type phases (a background assumption, not something I checked here). Ni-rich compositions went unmeasured on the assumption that they absorb light poorly.

| Index | Fe / Ni / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 158 | 0.53 / 0.18 / 0.29 | 1.72 µA |
| **34** | **0.39 / 0.18 / 0.42** | **2.80 µA** |
| 94 | 0.34 / 0.17 / 0.48 | 1.87 µA |

The best point is the one with Fe:V close to 1:1. Moving towards more Fe or more V lowered the photocurrent. That suggests a local peak near index 34, but three points don't show whether it's the best in the whole library.

I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements or read the known-phase list, which was too large to return in one go. So the phase explanation above is an assumption, not something I confirmed.
